title: Hijack Threat Note Grounds Kolkata-Mumbai Air India Flight Before Takeoff
excerpt: A threat found in the aircraft's washroom warning that the plane would be hijacked at 11:10 a.m. led officials to deboard all passengers and move the Mumbai-bound flight to an isolation bay at Kolkata airport on Wednesday morning.
body:
• A hijack threat note was found in the washroom of a Mumbai-bound Air India flight at Kolkata airport shortly before its scheduled 10:20 a.m. departure on Wednesday, November 11.
  • The note warned that the aircraft would be hijacked at 11:10 a.m., Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh told PTI.
  • All passengers who had boarded were deboarded, and the aircraft was moved to an isolation bay for a thorough security inspection.
  • Officials said security protocols were activated immediately and the threat was being assessed; no credible plot had been confirmed in the initial official account.

A Mumbai-bound Air India flight was moved to an isolation bay at Kolkata's Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport on Wednesday morning, November 11, after a hijack threat note was found in the aircraft's washroom shortly before takeoff, officials said. The flight had been scheduled to depart at 10:20 a.m.

What officials said

The note warned that the plane would be hijacked at 11:10 a.m., Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh told the Press Trust of India (PTI). All the passengers who had boarded the aircraft were deboarded, and the plane was taken to the isolation bay, Singh said. Security protocols were immediately activated, and the aircraft was moved to the isolation bay for a thorough inspection and necessary precautionary measures, he added.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=QxmXuRFweDw

"The flight had been scheduled to depart at 10:20 a.m."

The response

Singh's account describes the standard sequence for a threat of this kind: the passengers are taken off the aircraft, the plane is moved away from the terminal to an isolation bay, and security agencies search it before any decision is taken on the flight. That search was under way on Wednesday, and officials said the situation was being assessed.

Some reports put the number of passengers on board at 147 and described the message as written on a lavatory mirror. Those details were not part of the airport director's initial statement to PTI, and had not been officially confirmed in that account.

What is not yet known

Who wrote the note, and whether the threat was credible, remained unconfirmed in the initial official account. Authorities said further details were awaited as the assessment continued. There was no report in the official account of any suspect being identified, or of any object being found on the aircraft.

What happens next

The immediate question for passengers is when — and whether — the flight operates. That decision rests on the security checks Singh described: the aircraft can return to service only once agencies complete their inspection and clear it. Travellers booked on the Kolkata–Mumbai route on Wednesday should check their flight status with the airline, as a held aircraft and a deboarded passenger load typically mean a delayed or rescheduled departure.
